messages:
Priya (AE): Heads-up — BetaCorp POC hit repeated 429s during a customer demo and their sandbox free credits dropped to zero mid-run. The frontend hung. Can we swarm? :sweat_smile:
Diego (Solutions): ugh. Do we have the org id and which APIs they were calling? streaming chat or bulk embed?@Marta (Billing) fyi
Priya (AE): org=beta-ops-42, env=sandbox. They were running a streaming assistant + batched embeddings at the same time. Customer console shows ~950k tokens in 20m; their local SDK logs show ~420k.
Riley (SRE): sounds like duplicate consumption + retries. If their demo machine lost connectivity the client retry logic could be re-sending payloads. Any SDK code they used?
Priya (AE): they attached sample code (redacted):
```
// simplified
const rw = new Redwood({key:KEY});
await rw.chat.stream({model:'rw-medium', messages});
await rw.embeddings.create({model:'embed-1', input: docsBatch});
// wrapper auto-retries on socket close
```
They noted flaky hotel wifi.
spend-alert-bot: Spend alert: org=beta-ops-42 triggered at 1850012501 utc, free_credits_left=0, reason="free_credits_exhausted"
Marta (Billing): I see the alert. Free_credit_consumed=995123 tokens. I'll pause auto-invoice for now. Want me to grant a demo credit so they can finish?
Diego (Solutions): yes please — small credit and mute alerts briefly. Also we should give them a short explanation they can share with infra.
Riley (SRE): quick triage from our ingestion traces: we see repeated session reconnects with no idempotency metadata. Metering records show many near-duplicate token events clustered within seconds of reconnects. Example excerpt:
```
metertoken: org=beta-ops-42 id=null tokens=50123
metertoken: org=beta-ops-42 id=null tokens=49987
stream: reconnect idx=1
stream: reconnect idx=2
```
This implies client retries are counted as fresh tokens because there was no request-id to tie chunks together.
Priya (AE): customer asked if this is "a bug" on your side or theirs. Need a short plain-English note.
Marta (Billing): I applied a +200k token demo credit to beta-ops-42 and muted spend alerts for 45 minutes. billing system: credit_event{org:beta-ops-42, amount:200000, note:"POC support - demo retry noise"}
Riley (SRE): quick plain-English note: "During the live demo, the customer's device briefly lost connectivity. Their demo software retried streaming calls without a stable request identifier, which caused our metering to count the retried chunks as new usage. We added a temporary demo credit and muted alerts while they finished the test."
Diego (Solutions): can you also give two actionable items we can send?
Riley (SRE): sure — (1) short-term: set a unique X-RW-REQUEST-ID header for each logical operation (chat session or embed batch) so retries are idempotent; (2) avoid running large embed batches concurrently with streaming demos. We're also fast-tracking a server-side dedupe window.
Priya (AE): pinging the customer now with that text. They want to know timeline for a permanent fix.
Riley (SRE): plan/timeline: (A) accept client-provided idempotency header in canary — ETA 4 hours; (B) implement server-side 30s dedupe for streaming chunk tokens keyed by session-hash — ETA 2 days; (C) update POC playbook + quickstart example with an idempotency snippet — ETA 1 day. I'll open ticket POC-498 and link PRs.
Marta (Billing): noted on invoice annotation. I'll also earmark the 200k demo credit so it's clearly visible on their billing page.
Diego (Solutions): customer also asked for a code snippet they can drop into their demo app. Priya, we'll attach a tiny example in follow-up email and link to the playbook.
Priya (AE): customer re-ran the demo after credit and it completed successfully. They were relieved. They're asking for a short post-demo write-up we can share with their security/infra teams.
Riley (SRE): I'll produce a 1-paragraph postmortem and share in this channel once the canary deploys show no regressions. Leaving thread open for 24h to monitor. :thumbsup:
